\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آغاز} (āghāz)}{آغاز (āghāz)}]{\ur{آغاز} (āghāz) — a beginning}

\label{lesson:UR-C544-aghaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to put a value on, then the Urdu for correct.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آغاز}}
\textbf{\ur{آغاز}} — \emph{āghāz} — \textquotedblleft{}a beginning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آغاز} \ur{اچھا} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{آخر} \ur{بھی} \ur{اچھا} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āghāz achchhā huā to ākhir bhī achchhā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it starts well, it will end well too.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آغاز}} (\emph{āghāz}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{āghāz}, \textquotedblleft{}a beginning\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āghāz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āghāz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āghāz achchhā huā to ākhir bhī achchhā ho gā.} — If it starts well, it will end well too.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to put a value on, then the Urdu for correct, then say \emph{āghāz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{آغاز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A beginning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شروع} (shurū)}{شروع (shurū)}]{\ur{شروع} (shurū) — the start (shurū karnā: to begin)}

\label{lesson:UR-C544-shuru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for correct, then the Urdu for a beginning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شروع}}
\textbf{\ur{شروع}} — \emph{shurū} — \textquotedblleft{}the start (shurū karnā: to begin)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میچ} \ur{وقت} \ur{پر} \ur{شروع} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{دیکھیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar maich vaqt par shurū huā to ham dekheṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شروع}} (\emph{shurū}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{shurūʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}setting about, beginning\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اختتام} (ikhtitām)}{اختتام (ikhtitām)}]{\ur{اختتام} (ikhtitām) — the close (of an event)}

\label{lesson:UR-C544-ikhtitam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a beginning, then the Urdu for the start.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اختتام}}
\textbf{\ur{اختتام}} — \emph{ikhtitām} — \textquotedblleft{}the close (of an event)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{اختتام} \ur{پر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{سوال} \ur{پوچھیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ikhtitām par vaqt huā to ham savāl pūchheṅ ge.}

Masculine.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سلسلہ} (silsilā)}{سلسلہ (silsilā)}]{\ur{سلسلہ} (silsilā) — a series; a run (of events)}

\label{lesson:UR-C544-silsila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the start, then the Urdu for the close (of an event).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سلسلہ}}
\textbf{\ur{سلسلہ}} — \emph{silsilā} — \textquotedblleft{}a series; a run (of events)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{کا} \ur{سلسلہ} \ur{جاری} \ur{رہا} \ur{تو} \ur{سیلاب} \ur{آئے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish kā silsilā jārī rahā to sailāb āe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the rain keeps on, there will be a flood.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سلسلہ}} (\emph{silsilā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{silsila}, \textquotedblleft{}a chain\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ترتیب} (tartīb)}{ترتیب (tartīb)}]{\ur{ترتیب} (tartīb) — order (a set sequence)}

\label{lesson:UR-C544-tartib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the close (of an event), then the Urdu for a series.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ترتیب}}
\textbf{\ur{ترتیب}} — \emph{tartīb} — \textquotedblleft{}order (a set sequence)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{کتابیں} \ur{ترتیب} \ur{سے} \ur{ہوتیں} \ur{تو} \ur{جلدی} \ur{ملتیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar kitābeṅ tartīb se hotīṅ to jaldī miltīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ترتیب}} (\emph{tartīb}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tartīb}, \textquotedblleft{}arranging in order\textquotedblright{}.
